 LUMINA: K-pop group created entirely by AI attracts over 3 million views.
 A four-member K-pop girl group, created entirely by artificial intelligence (AI), is gaining attention in South Korea after their debut music video surpassed 3 million views on YouTube in about five weeks since its release.
 Đài Phát thanh và Truyền hình Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh • 14/11/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 When a securities firm builds a virtual band
 According to Reuters, Samsung Securities developed LUMINA to create virtual faces for the company's social media content. The group consists of four virtual members, with their debut song titled "Override." The entire song, characters, and music video were created using AI. 
 Uhm Sewon, a representative from Samsung Securities' communications strategy department, stated that the company produces approximately 1,500 pieces of content annually and faces difficulties in finding suitable people to appear on camera. While professional staff are unfamiliar with presenting content, hiring celebrities is expensive and may not necessarily align with the brand image. 
 The virtual girl group LUMINA consists of four members created entirely by AI (Photo: Samsung Securities) 
 You may also like Thanks to advancements in technology, LUMINA's dance moves have become increasingly natural. After about five weeks since its release, the "Override" music video has surpassed 3 million views on YouTube, receiving much positive feedback from viewers regarding its visuals and music .
 Samsung Securities stated that it will continue to develop content centered around the group, including performance videos , new songs, member interviews, short video challenges, and investment education programs. The company also publicly identified LUMINA as a fictional character created using AI and subject financial-related content to multiple professional review processes to ensure accuracy.
 AI presents both opportunities and challenges for the music industry.
 The emergence of LUMINA reflects the increasingly evident trend of AI application in the South Korean entertainment industry. However, experts have also raised concerns about the rights of creators as the technology could replace some jobs related to performing, producing, and composing music. 
 Uhm Sewon, Head of Communications Strategy at Samsung Securities, who was in charge of producing the music video for "Override" by the virtual K-pop group LUMINA, is interviewed by Reuters at Samsung Electronics headquarters in Seoul, South Korea, on October 23, 2026 (Photo: Reuters). 
 You may also like Park Sang-cheol, president of the Korean Singers Association, believes AI can help reduce production costs and assist artists during rehearsals. However, he warns that this technology risks impacting the work of musicians, songwriters, arrangers, and advertising models. The use of AI-generated images and voices also raises the need to protect the rights of creators.
 According to Park, live performances still have their own value thanks to the personality, emotions, and interaction between the artist and the audience – elements that AI can hardly replace completely.
 Unlike some previous virtual music groups where the vocals or performances were handled by humans, LUMINA was created entirely using AI. The project is therefore not just a marketing experiment for the company, but also contributes to a new perspective on the future boundaries between technology and artistic creation.
 Source: Reuters
